builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SEER: A Scalable Event-Driven Runtime for Parallel Execution of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Environments
summary: SEER replaces the serial CPU-side env.step path of vectorized MARL environments with a bounded event-driven runtime using a CAS-based dual-layer queue and preflight-guided thread-pool sizing, so independent entity events execute in parallel while preserving serial-equivalent step semantics. Adoption costs a rewrite of the environment under an explicit event-locality contract (entity-local direct updates, cross-entity effects as ordered future events) plus the complexity of a custom parallel runtime, with no gain in memory or model quality. It can fail if the environment does not satisfy the locality contract, if workloads are not interaction-intensive enough to amortize scheduling overhead, or if subtle ordering bugs break serial-equivalence guarantees that training correctness depends on.
rationale: The approach is sound but only pays off for interaction-heavy MARL training at scale, requires re-architecting existing environments under a strict contract, and offers nothing to engineers whose workloads are LLM inference or standard single-agent RL.

claims.statement: SEER replaces the serial CPU-side env.step path of vectorized MARL environments with a bounded event-driven runtime using a CAS-based dual-layer queue and preflight-guided thread-pool sizing, so independent entity events execute in parallel while preserving serial-equivalent step semantics. Adoption costs a rewrite of the environment under an explicit event-locality contract (entity-local direct updates, cross-entity effects as ordered future events) plus the complexity of a custom parallel runtime, with no gain in memory or model quality. It can fail if the environment does not satisfy the locality contract, if workloads are not interaction-intensive enough to amortize scheduling overhead, or if subtle ordering bugs break serial-equivalence guarantees that training correctness depends on.

Reduces environment-execution latency by 46.9%, 19.5%, and 64.9% over ROSS-T, NBSE, and ROOT-Sim respectively on a communication-intensive MARL workload; 16.2% inference-latency reduction on a UAV swarm workload.
